faqs.question: What does the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the IgM antibodies in your blood.

faqs.question: Why is the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fifth disease or slapped cheek syndrome in children • To determine if a pregnant woman has been exposed to the virus • To identify hydrops fetalis, a rare complication of pregnancy caused by the virus

faqs.question: When is the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor might recommend this test if • you show symptoms of the fifth disease, such as fever, rash, headache, etc., • you are a pregnant woman who may have been exposed to the virus, or • your newborn baby shows symptoms of hydrops fetalis.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: A positive result indicates recent or current infection with the virus. High antibody levels can show that the infection was recent, and low levels can suggest previous exposure to the virus.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test?
faqs.answer: A healthcare professional will collect a blood sample from your vein using a needle. They will send to a laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor if you're taking any medications that can affect your immune system and if you have any specific requirements. • You may be asked to schedule the test for later if you have cold or flu-like symptoms.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test?
faqs.answer: • Parvovirus B19 IgG Antibody Test: This test detects exposure to parvovirus B19 and can differentiate current from past infections. • Complete Blood Count: This blood test measures various parameters of blood cells and can help diagnose complications of parvovirus infection.

faqs.question: What is the Parvovirus B19 IgM Antibody test also known as?
faqs.answer: Parvo IgM or B19V IgM or Slapped cheek syndrome test

faqs.question: What is Fifth disease or slapped cheek syndrome?
faqs.answer: Fifth disease or slapped cheek syndrome is a mild viral illness commonly seen in children, caused by the human parvovirus B19. It usually causes a mild rash on the face and body and resolves without treatment.
